ankle_flex.source: Seated calf raise guides (Gravitus, BODi): lower until the heels drop 2 to 3 inches below the platform for a full stretch (illustrative 15 degrees of dorsiflexion); push up onto the toes as high as possible (illustrative -35 degrees of plantar flexion). No exact angle is given, so both ends are illustrative, inside the AAOS ankle row

knee_flex.source: Seated calf raise guides (Gravitus, BODi): the knees sit under the padded lever the whole set; use only the ankle joint and avoid lifting with the knees or hips, a narrow band around the seated 90-degree knee angle

muscles.peakSource: Seated calf raise guides: hold the fully contracted position briefly (1 to 2 seconds) at the top to maximize muscle engagement, so effort is highest through that hold

mistake.name: Bounce and shortchange it

tells.text: The heels bounce off the bottom stretch instead of pausing there.
The rise stops halfway instead of reaching full plantar flexion.

mistake.source: Seated calf raise mistake guides (Hevy, Livestrong): bouncing at the bottom uses elastic rebound instead of muscle contraction; a partial range of motion that rises only halfway activates only part of the calf's muscle fibers

sources: Contact fact (knee pad / footplate): balls of the feet on the footplate with heels hanging off the edge, hip-width apart, toes forward; the padded lever rests just above the knees (Gravitus)
